reviews.text: You can’t fault the energy level but, unfortunately, the action and the comedy frequently get in each other’s way.
reviews.author: Geoffrey Macnab

reviews.text: The King’s Man is clearly not perfect, but it retains some of the best elements of its predecessors, adds enough new lore to justify itself as a prequel, and is a fun, entertaining film on its own.
reviews.author: Joseph Tomastik

reviews.text: “The King’s Man” may be my favorite entry in a problematic franchise. I always preferred Colin Firth to Taron Egerton. The prequel tricks audiences into accepting the fifty-nine-year-old, single and child free Fiennes as the protagonist and an action star
reviews.author: Sarah Vincent

reviews.text: For a prequel that promised something large, loud, and ostensibly entertaining, the movie just doesn’t quite suit up.
reviews.author: Nadine Whitney

reviews.text: Awesome action & memorable characters… but left me with a story that wasn’t my cup of tea…
reviews.author: Zach Pope

reviews.text: In this secret service spy prequel, director Matthew Vaughn meanders his way into the First World War to revise history, but he appears to have forgotten to revise the script.
reviews.author: Ryan Oquiza

reviews.text: The King's Man takes [the franchise] and boils it down to its most sensible origin story, delivering jaw-dropping twists, epic fights, and proving that over-the-top nonsense is sometimes all you need.
reviews.author: Maggie Lovitt

reviews.text: Keeping on needlessly keeping on: that's still this spy series' main trait, as it always has been.
reviews.author: Sarah Ward

reviews.text: From the first minute to the end of its long two hours, The King’s Man is pure climax with an incessant grandiloquent score; or better yet, a climax without a clear thread that may make you faint. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Javier Ocaña

reviews.text:
Simply put, it lacks a sense of fun.
[Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Ruben Peralta Rigaud

reviews.text: Funnier, more surprising, and more heartfelt than the first two films in the series, and if the team can keep up this level of quality in the future, then Mr. Bond may just have to watch his back.
reviews.author: Dan Bayer

reviews.text: Can't decide if it wants to be Paths of Glory or Austin Powers.
reviews.author: Kip Mooney

reviews.text: Unlike RoboCop 3 or Police Academy III: Back in Training, The King's Man retains the R rating of its predecessors, though here it feels like the MPA is primarily trying to protect children from boredom.
reviews.author: Bill Chambers

reviews.text: With all of the excitement of the Kingsman franchise so far, this was a bit of an over-historic dud.
reviews.author: Vincent Schilling

reviews.text: As a stand-alone film, The Kings Man is decent but doesnt stray far from other war/spy films. However, as part of the Kingsman franchise...
reviews.author: Allison Rose

reviews.text: Vaughns "The Kings Man" explores the inevitability of man-made death and why those with the means have a responsibility to prevent it, not for glory but because its the right thing to do. For all its dour presentation, theres a persistent hope ...
reviews.author: Douglas Davidson

reviews.text: The King's Man has its moments, but it also has a lot of flaws. Fiennes and Ifans steal the show, but the disconnected story makes it feel like two completely different movies.
reviews.author: Tessa Smith

reviews.text: The King’s Man sets up the story of the British patriotic spy ring using a high-end clothier as its front -- but instead of dapper pinstripes, this one’s dressed in a clown suit.
reviews.author: John Serba

reviews.text: It's all great fun, full of sly humour, snappy action and dapper dressing.
reviews.author: Terry Staunton

reviews.text: Most of what made the original Kingsman a fun ride is largely lost in the prequel, which can't juggle the tone of campy, comic book theatrics, and the humbling, solemn WWI elements.
reviews.author: Jeffrey Harris

reviews.text: When you can't take the villain seriously it's hard to have any stakes within the film. The only enjoyment was the action which was barely sub par.
reviews.author: Brandon Avery

reviews.text: Still enough energy to make it enjoyable but the are really squeezing every entertainment drop out of the franchise.
reviews.author: Jackie K. Cooper

reviews.text: Although it doesn't have the panache and zing of that first film, the swordplay and fight choreography are as impressive as before.
reviews.author: Lynn Venhaus

reviews.text: Earnest prequel to the earlier knockabout films, it is somehow at odds with itself, spluttering to life under the spell of Ifans' Rasputin but doesn't get going till the end
reviews.author: Jane Freebury

reviews.text: Even if you haven't seen the other Kingsman movies, I think you can watch this on its own merit.
reviews.author: Tony Baker

reviews.text: A film to pass the time... but nothing more. You better watch it without high expectations; otherwise, you may not have such a good time. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Sebastian Zavala Kahn

reviews.text: An action movie that wants to be something else. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Hernán Ferreirós

reviews.text: The King's Man is noble to a fault and preachy at its worst moments. The polished lacquer of its slick, suave spy adventure shows a bit of tarnish that comes with its age and overuse.
reviews.author: Caitlin Kennedy

reviews.text: Although The King's Man continues to maintain a peculiar sense of humor, its tone is less exaggerated and more dramatic. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Denise Pieniazek

reviews.text: A film that's lost all its charm. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Diego Batlle

reviews.text: I had to wait a long while forThe King's Manto become a good movie. But it does get there eventually.
reviews.author: Alan Ng

reviews.text: [Matthew Vaughn] doesn't take his foot off the gas for a second. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Pablo O. Scholz

reviews.text: The King's Man is far from enough to save a flagging franchise.
reviews.author: Joel Fisher

reviews.text: Afterwards I had to check if, for example, Mata Hari seduced US president Woodrow Wilson. This did-it-happen? question holds the interest throughout what is otherwise just another well-made, well-acted spy caper.
reviews.author: Stephen Romei

reviews.text: It's hard to exactly pinpoint where The King's Man has gone awry, but, despite a clever early twist, it just all feels ploddingly predictable in a join-the-dots-of-history and Kingsman origin-tale kind of way.
reviews.author: James Croot

reviews.text: An intriguing, absorbing, well-crafted adventure story that offers real excitement, tragedy, emotional drama, and characters who are well-rounded and believable that we can actually believe and invest in.
reviews.author: Paul Mount

reviews.text: Awkwardly combining playful quirks and historical references with brutal violence and revisionist conspiracy theories, this intermittently stirring adventure takes on a sketchy quality in which only a fraction of the snippets spark to life.
reviews.author: Todd Jorgenson

reviews.text: Its fantastical comic-book mentality merging with the boldness of re-writing historical events and figureheads lends The King's Man enough of a pass to be deemed more worthy than it deserves
reviews.author: Peter Gray

reviews.text: The King's Man and its confused vision feels like a dissident shadow of the bright, creative spark behind its predecessors.
reviews.author: Matt Conway

reviews.text: Tonally and thematically The King's Man is all over the place, in a way that lays bare the cynicism of Vaughn's own mission: to appear transgressive yet reassuringly conventional.
reviews.author: Jake Wilson

reviews.text: Keep your expectations low with this one.
reviews.author: Matthew Toomey

reviews.text: A somewhat tedious war drama. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Janire Zurbano

reviews.text: You keep waiting for The King's Man to find its footing.
reviews.author: Mark Meszoros

reviews.text: Absurdly frenzied prequel with a convoluted script that's tonally inconsistent and, therefore, confusing.
reviews.author: Susan Granger

reviews.text: There be no two ways about it: the film is pure pulp; beautifully prepared and served, it's a B-grade adventure movie with A-grade storytelling, including a series of splendid twists with an absolute beaut that will snap any audience into stunned silence.
reviews.author: Jim Schembri

reviews.text: Such a baffling movie that's tonally off. It started out serious but then became a self parody, especially the scenes involving Rhys Ifans. Even a committed performance from Ralph Fiennes can't save this movie.
reviews.author: Ruth Maramis

reviews.text: The King's Man shines brightest when it references its own origins. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mariona Borrull

reviews.text: Vaughn stages long, rollicking sequences in which sudden new events keep on coming.
reviews.author: Edward Porter

reviews.text: Forgiving a few storytelling missteps, The King's Man is in line to be one of the year's best.
reviews.author: Rhys Bowen Jones

reviews.text: I'm not sure that the Kingsman franchise, through its first two films, generated quite enough lore to justify a prequel
reviews.author: Stephen Silver

reviews.text: Surprising script decisions... are brave and bring much more character to the piece than other films in the series. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Jorge Loser

reviews.text: All of Matthew Vaughn's personalities came out to write a script, at one time.
reviews.author: Korey Coleman

reviews.text: The first film was a delightfully nasty surprise, its sequel a bit of a retread. The King's Man feels like it's having an identity crisis, unsure whether or not to grow up or stick to its gleefully bloody ways.
reviews.author: Cory Woodroof

reviews.text: It's meant as a prequel grandfather to the two previous films, but it has so little connection to the other two in tone, wit, and style, at best it's a very distant cousin, twice removed. Too bad they didn't go for a third.
reviews.author: Piers Marchant

reviews.text: Credit must be given to director and co-writer Matthew Vaughn for swerving into fresh territory when he could have made this a safe, lazy rehash.
reviews.author: John Lui

reviews.text: There's the potential for an exhilarating adventure, but it's just too uneven to hold the attention.
reviews.author: Rich Cline

reviews.text: Vaughn stages his action scenes with verve, while creating wacky alternate versions of historical events.
reviews.author: Andy Lea

reviews.text: The tone lurches awkwardly from sweeping colonial melodrama to grim battle epic, camp, pseudo-Bond caper and crass, unfunny farce.
reviews.author: Simran Hans

reviews.text: This is an action movie that feels too long because it was really over before even hitting the middle section.
reviews.author: Alci Rengifo

reviews.text: To borrow from the Indian philosopher Chanakya, it is better to be without a 'Kingsman' than to have a bad one.
reviews.author: Brian Lloyd

reviews.text: The King's Man is a marked improvement because, while mildly jingoistic, it plays the old empire card with tongue planted firmly in cheek.
reviews.author: Paul Whitington

reviews.text: An audacious take on history which wildly varies in tone; if you can loosen up and enjoy it as a historical fantasia it can be fun.
reviews.author: Peter Canavese

reviews.text: It's only in the story's final throws where the film seem to remember it's a Kingsman movie and starts actually having fun, but by then it's too little too late...
reviews.author: Jennifer Heaton

reviews.text: ...it's hard to find a consistent flavour in a two-faced film that revels in gleeful slaughter in the action scenes and then po-faced renditions of war poetry by contrast...
reviews.author: Eddie Harrison

reviews.text: Our Managing Editor's look at The King's Man, a surprisingly ineffectual addition to the KM saga that wastes some pretty mighty talent along the way.
reviews.author: Jason Gorber

reviews.text: The script lacks the humor of the first two films and frankly is missing the actor Taron Edgerton.
reviews.author: Sarah Knight Adamson

reviews.text: The King's Man might have succeeded better if it hadn't so frequently resorted to so much bawdy humor
reviews.author: Steven Prokopy

reviews.text: The story has roots in early movie adventure, with sword fights, extreme scenic headquarters, true evil doers and a spectacular airplane stunt. That's enough for the KINGSMEN!
reviews.author: Patrick McDonald

reviews.text: just enough of what the "get your mind off things" cinematic doctor ordered. Perhaps a second viewing would yield a different critique, but in its time and place when I saw it, "The King's Man" was entertainingly diverting enough.
reviews.author: Jim Judy

reviews.text: The King's Man feels as though it is splintering off in all directions, as though it's three movies spliced-and-diced into one, messy sequel-ready story.
reviews.author: Richard Crouse

reviews.text: I actually like it quite a bit, despite some reservations about the tone.
reviews.author: Wade Major

reviews.text: The King's Man is a completely different animal than its predecessors, and it's better for it...be prepared for something equally as entertaining, but completely changed.
reviews.author: Damond Fudge

reviews.text: The previous installments were good but not great, a mostly forgettable fun time, and this prequel is no exception... but the door is left open just a crack if the demand materializes for Kingsman Begins.
reviews.author: Kevin A. Ranson

reviews.text: It's starting to become clear that the success of the 2014 original has been a blessing and a curse, with writer/director Matthew Vaughn desperately trying to capture the formula that made that first film such a success but failing miserably.
reviews.author: Micheal Compton

reviews.text: The King's Man is an off-putting installment in a series that should have already ended.
reviews.author: Brianna Zigler

reviews.text: By the end of the movie they give you that tone you're looking for, but it's a little late.
reviews.author: Lonita Cook

reviews.text: The unusual mix of revisionist history with The Kingman's energy works. The real surprise is how much emotional weight it delivers.
reviews.author: Sean Chandler

reviews.text: It's an affront to all.
reviews.author: Chris Knight

reviews.text: It is downright diabolical for Vaughn to make audiences even imagine a sequel to this unnecessary prequel simply to see if can be as outlandish as promised.
reviews.author: Mark Olsen

reviews.text: As either a 007-inspired spy film or a comic book adventure, The King's Man feels stale.
reviews.author: James Berardinelli

reviews.text: It's weirdly uneven. It doesn't have great focus; it's a real mixed bag... But I didn't hate it.
reviews.author: Kevin Carr

reviews.text: "The King's Man" can't shake the gross immaturity and sneakily conservative messaging of the franchise.
reviews.author: Hoai-Tran Bui

reviews.text: You could celebrate the season watching Ralph Fiennes in one of the dumbest movies of the year, but why would you want to?
reviews.author: Norman Wilner

reviews.text: Part satire, part adventure, this prequel fails at both...
reviews.author: Richard Roeper

reviews.text: For the most part, though, the film has such a sloppy but fun narrative that one imagines the expansive cast...
reviews.author: Adam Mullins-Khatib

reviews.text: A new take on WWI, done in the way I would've wanted it in school...
reviews.author: Shawn Edwards

reviews.text: Fiennes is as charming as ever. But it's also hard not to wish he had a better movie than this to exhibit both his singular charisma and combat skills.
reviews.author: Lindsey Bahr

reviews.text: The prequel is still entertaining and an improvement on the sequel, but neither have been able to live up to the fresh and unique tone set by the first film.
reviews.author: Paul McGuire Grimes

reviews.text: While he capably masters the superhero-like feats of Orlando and the team, Vaughn mixes in heavy emotional events that seem startlingly out of place in this type of movie. The result is a wildly uneven production.
reviews.author: Jonathan W. Hickman

reviews.text: A dumb bit of fun, a revisionist history of WWI told in a nimble, comic-book style.... Rasputin (Rhys Ifans) is deliciously over-the-top, albeit in a pretty spectacular way.
reviews.author: Gary M. Kramer

reviews.text: A juvenile mash-up of history, spoof and outlandish action that's simultaneously tin-eared and smug...Movies garble history all the time, but few have done so to such grotesque effect.
reviews.author: Frank Swietek

reviews.text: Any movie that lists "Rasputin dance choreographer" in the credits deserves at least a look.
reviews.author: Jeannette Catsoulis

reviews.text: A charismatic cast and occasionally entertaining piece of action choreography keep it from complete tedium, but this odd hybrid of war drama and patriotic action orgy never finds its groove.
reviews.author: Brian Tallerico

reviews.text: A dreary knock-off in period costume that doubles as an embarrassing work of wish fulfillment for anyone who just wishes Bond could be more overtly royalist.
reviews.author: Jen Chaney

reviews.text: I honestly don't see how The King's Man isn't the final nail in this series' cinematic coffin.
reviews.author: Sara Michelle Fetters

reviews.text: All the broad humor of the original film is gone, replaced by clunky and often tasteless gags, and the attempts to extract pathos from genuine tragedies vary from tacky to insulting.
reviews.author: Richard Whittaker

reviews.text: History is just one big playpen for "The King's Man," but some games are less fun than others.
reviews.author: Mark Feeney

reviews.text: "The King's Man" has gravitas, if a movie in which Ralph Fiennes is licked by a goat can be said to have gravitas.
reviews.author: Rob Thomas

reviews.text: A nonsensical comics-based Brit spy thriller set in the early 1900s.
reviews.author: Dennis Schwartz

reviews.text: The film is all over the place, stumbling mightily in the beginning, but steadily builds momentum from some spectacular fight sequences that snowball into an insanely good time.
reviews.author: Louisa Moore

reviews.text: The King's Man is a charmless prequel that's messier than the unkempt beard and head of hair on Rasputin, the movie's flashiest villain. Even with a talented cast, this [movie] gets bogged down in a jumbled plot and cringeworthy dialogue.
reviews.author: Carla Hay

reviews.text: [I]t's difficult to trust co-writer/director Matthew Vaughn's new approach to and tone within this installment.
reviews.author: Mark Dujsik

reviews.text: It's hard to quit the "Kingsman" series, though they're seemingly trying to force us out.
reviews.author: Johnny Oleksinski

reviews.text: It all builds to a satisfying, at-times breathtaking climax that is some of the best Vaughn has put on screen.
reviews.author: Kevin L. Lee

reviews.text: The King's Man should satisfy fans of the earlier movies, who come in knowing what to expect. Others might want to check them out first.
reviews.author: Daniel M. Kimmel

reviews.text: A strange sort of Frankenstein's monster that will frustrate people that both liked and disliked the original Kingsman, and completely fail to find an audience of its own.
reviews.author: Grant Watson

reviews.text: 'The King's Man' is tonally erratic, jumping around from comedy to farce, to violence and tragedy.
reviews.author: Bob Bloom

reviews.text: Don't let its handsome tailoring fool you; it's a mess.
reviews.author: Adam Graham

reviews.text: The third Kingsman film is quite enjoyable at times. It is uneven, as there is a lot Vaughn is trying to do, but it works best when the action is at the forefront.
reviews.author: Austin Burke

reviews.text: Who could not give themselves over to a scene in which, as Rasputin, Rhys Ifans - the film's lethal secret weapon - duels balletically with the heroes to the strains of the 1812 overture?
reviews.author: Donald Clarke

reviews.text: Fiennes is elegant and charming throughout "King's Man," unflappable in the face of perils that would flap anybody else, but his light touch often seems to be in the wrong movie.
reviews.author: Chris Hewitt

reviews.text: However noble Vaughn's intentions with "The King's Man," the film itself doesn't deliver on what it promises, either as an action movie or a wartime drama.
reviews.author: Sean P. Means

reviews.text: This prequel to Kingsman: The Secret Service and Kingsman: The Golden Circle is almost nothing like its predecessors. Even if it wasn't an overlong, tedious bore, the shift in tone would be enough to confound fans of the series.
reviews.author: Mike McGranaghan

reviews.text: The King's Man is a deeply weird film, albeit one tethered to reality by Fiennes and Dickinson's stiff-upper-lip sensibility.
reviews.author: Sonny Bunch

reviews.text: The King's Man tackles the horrific side of war with a serious bent while still maintaining the franchise's elements of humor, action, and adventure.
reviews.author: Danielle Solzman

reviews.text: While the loopy emphasis throughout on fine tailoring offers some amusement, as does the presence of some very feisty goats, this plays like a grudgingly completed job for hire for all involved.
reviews.author: Leslie Felperin

reviews.text: Vaughn's stylistic signature of balletic brutality is among the film's pleasures, although the narrative's hybrid tone - part academic, part acid trip - is not.
reviews.author: Michael O'Sullivan

reviews.text: The King's Man is a movie that the filmmakers think is doing some deep work yet it feels like a lazy sequel in a franchise that never needed to be one.
reviews.author: Julian Lytle

reviews.text: As toxically regressive in its politics as it is impeccable in its tailoring,The King's Manis a jaunty, ludicrous romp through an alternative history of pre-World War II Europe.
reviews.author: Oliver Jones

reviews.text: The franchise pivots in a totally different direction, but a fun one - sort of a British Inglorious Basterds, rewriting history. The anti-war message is also very compelling.
reviews.author: Grace Randolph

reviews.text: Somewhere along the line, the Kingsman films stopped being fun.
reviews.author: Tom Santilli

reviews.text: Matthew Vaughn's ambitiously lopsided piece of revisionist history "The King's Man" is a pointless, half-hazard entry in a dormant franchise struggling for relevance.
reviews.author: Nate Adams

reviews.text: The King's Man gives a noble effort to be more refined than its predecessor, but due to its identity crisis, it leaves much to be desired.
reviews.author: Rendy Jones

reviews.text: This movie is a boring mess that drags on and on, with blips of interest scattered across its interminable 131 minutes.
reviews.author: Rob Dean

reviews.text: I gotta say I was blown away... This is a more "grown-up" movie.
reviews.author: Jaby Koay

reviews.text: It's disjointed, feels unnecessary, and is only sporadically entertaining. The twists are either too much or too obvious and its connections to the franchise are wholly uninspired.
reviews.author: Germain Lussier

reviews.text: Not nearly as thrilling as it should be, this origin story to the Kingsman franchise is elevated by a superb Ralph Fiennes and, well, relative action.
reviews.author: Thom Ernst

reviews.text: Lacking cohesion and consistency, it isn't going to win new fans, let alone appease existing ones.
reviews.author: Katie Smith-Wong

reviews.text: "The King's Man" is a mess, purposeless, pointless, witless.
reviews.author: Mick LaSalle

reviews.text: This origins story is a little bit schizophrenic, and a little bit fun.
reviews.author: Joanna Langfield

reviews.text: The King's Man is a fantastic adventure with thrilling action as sharp as its style and wit.
reviews.author: Mark McPherson

reviews.text: Despite a clever, history-subverting idea and a few great action sequences, this overlong, mostly needless prequel flails all over the place, pretending to decry violence but actually thriving on it.
reviews.author: Jeffrey M. Anderson

reviews.text: Although Matthew Vaughn's shake-up of the franchise's status-quo aesthetic might cause some to bid a farewell to "Kingsman," those willing to make the turn with him will find plenty to enjoy in this more muted and erudite action fantasia.
reviews.author: Nick Rogers

reviews.text: [Even] with all the jarring tonal shifts that alternate between the serious/revisionist historical war epic and the tongue-in-cheek action-comedy vibe, 'The King's Man' is far from a total disaster.
reviews.author: Casey Chong

reviews.text: The King's Man's charming sense of adventure and surprisingly heady topics leave the film overstuffed -- but it's still a fun experience.
reviews.author: Brandon Zachary

reviews.text: In a seriocomic prequel to his hit Kingsman action comedies, director Matthew Vaughn celebrates manly ideals of sacrifice and service -- and Fiennes embodies them with gusto. He holds the film together.
reviews.author: Michael Sragow

reviews.text: Under the perfect tailoring there's an ugly edge, a cynicism that would shock even Bond, and that makes it very hard to cheer on this King or his men.
reviews.author: Helen O'Hara

reviews.text: A spirited adventure perfectly suited to popcorn.
reviews.author: Anne Brodie

reviews.text: Watching "The King's Man" is like being bludgeoned with a bowler hat.
reviews.author: Russ Simmons

reviews.text: The script written by Vaughn himself with Karl Gajdusek is very inspired, providing just the right touch between danger and comedy. [Full review in Spanish]
reviews.author: Mikel Zorrilla

reviews.text: But Fiennes is dependably great and as long as the action and thrills are in the foreground, "The King's Man" is all the silly fun you've come to expect from this series.
reviews.author: Mathew DeKinder

reviews.text: I had a lot more fun than I expected to. If this is your introduction to the franchise, I don't think it will hit as hard for you.
reviews.author: Dan Murrell

reviews.text: Neither lighthearted enough to evoke the breezy thrills of the first two films nor consistently serious enough to give them a truly substantive historical or emotional foundation. It's also a tiresome slog.
reviews.author: Todd Gilchrist

reviews.text: There are some truly bizarre set pieces, but a sudden shift into serious melodrama with a Gallipoli-style depiction of the horrors of trench warfare serves only to highlight the film's utter tastelessness.
reviews.author: Alistair Harkness

reviews.text: The King's Man is a wickedly creative origin story. It swings wildly from violent to hysterical with gut punch surprises.
reviews.author: Julian Roman

reviews.text: Unfortunately, the movie does have to devolve into what it says on the tin, a manic and frantic action thriller with less panache than either of its two predecessors.
reviews.author: Dominic Griffin

reviews.text: In all, the film is a much more enjoyable installment than the second film and deeper than the first one. Fans of the franchise will need to come with an open mind to embrace the third film's more emotionally-ladened tone in order to enjoy it.
reviews.author: Joshua Mackey

reviews.text: An enjoyably action-packed prequel
reviews.author: Chris Bumbray

reviews.text: The King's Man is a major disappointment. Instead of being a thrilling new chapter, one filling in the blanks, it just sticks out like a sore thumb with how unnecessary it is.
reviews.author: Joey Magidson

reviews.text: Fiennes, of course, is typically impressive throughout, sword-fighting, punching, shooting, kicking and crying his over-stretched heart out, giving everything, desperately trying, hoping it seems, to wrestle greatness from tedium. If only.
reviews.author: Kevin Maher

reviews.text: Occasionally comes alive with excitement, but it's more of a dull and overly dramatic World War I movie featuring a father and son butting heads over honor and reputation
reviews.author: Robert Kojder

reviews.text: Vaughn, in his excitement, often fails to create a balanced picture, offering an occasionally rough ride of tonal highs and lows.
reviews.author: Brian Orndorf

reviews.text: The King's Man is a big-screen experience with plenty of whizz-bang about it.
reviews.author: James Mottram

reviews.text: The King's Man is a worthy prequel that cleverly utilizes its war-set period to establish greater stakes.
reviews.author: Ben Rolph

reviews.text: It is never boring, but it is also never remotely consistent in its sensibilities and vision.
reviews.author: Barry Hertz

reviews.text: Its plot and tone each end up zig-zagging manically in the attempt to fulfil both the film's creative ambitions and its duties to the brand.
reviews.author: Robbie Collin

reviews.text: A muddled, unfunny and overlong mess which is only slightly elevated by a peerless central performance courtesy of Fiennes
reviews.author: Linda Marric

reviews.text: Believe it or not, the one crucial thing you need to understand about The King's Man is it has the most delightfully batshit fight scene you'll see at the cinema this year. And that, dear reader, is worth the price of admission.
reviews.author: David Crow

reviews.text: The King's Man is better action and team-dynamic fun than we've seen from the Kingsman franchise so far, at the somewhat heavy cost of some overly serious and dark wartime drama.
reviews.author: Kofi Outlaw

reviews.text: In a nutshell, Matthew Vaughn's trilogy has imploded and the fizzy combo of Taron Egerton and Colin Firth is sorely missed.
reviews.author: Charlotte O'Sullivan

reviews.text: For all its faults, The King's Man is at least hilariously bad in the way that emotionless, made-by-committee blockbusters like Star Wars: The Rise of Skywalker are not.
reviews.author: Christian Holub

reviews.text: Fun in places, this World War I era story was designed to expand the franchise but appears just as likely to end it.
reviews.author: Brian Lowry

reviews.text: The Kingsman franchise is really a test of what audiences are willing to put up with in exchange for a handful of cool action scenes.
reviews.author: Clarisse Loughrey

reviews.text: Gleeful, gruesome violence has been one of the more memorable aspects of the Kingsman movies; one is sad to say that, outside of a grungy, late-in-the-film battle royale in a World War I no-man's-land, there just isn't enough of it here.
reviews.author: Ignatiy Vishnevetsky

reviews.text: Once the film's second half gets under way, which is overwhelmed with convoluted plot developments, chintzy CGI, and hollow triumphs, it's easy to forget everyone's motivations.
reviews.author: Vikram Murthi

reviews.text: This blend of serious war film, boys' own adventure and preposterous comedy has its moments, but it's a strange brew that ultimately falls a little flat.
reviews.author: Anna Smith

reviews.text: Vaughn gets a lot of points for imagination, but then quite a lot taken away for not knowing when to stop. A blast at times, The King's Man could have sacrificed a fair chunk of plot for a bit more comedy.
reviews.author: Olly Richards

reviews.text: The King's Man's triumphant action and epic performances are dragged down by a confused story and overlong runtime.
reviews.author: Rosie Knight

reviews.text: Though it has a healthy sense of humor about its own outlandishness, 'King's Man' is impossibly silly and disposable nonetheless.
reviews.author: Charles Bramesco

reviews.text: In the way of the First World War which it chronicles, there simply aren't enough good men or women to throw at The King's Man who could ever make a difference.
reviews.author: Fionnuala Halligan

reviews.text: The results may turn some Kingsman fans off, but those willing to embrace this entry's greater thematic and stylistic ambitions will find much to savor, including the stirring lead performance by Ralph Fiennes.
reviews.author: Frank Scheck

reviews.text: 'The King's Man' feels like Matthew Vaughn very much wanting to tell a World War I-set action spy drama and using the established brand as a commercial justification.
reviews.author: Scott Mendelson

reviews.text: It alternates between trying to copy James Bond and Austin Powers; is this supposed to be a sincere action film or a total spoof?
reviews.author: Mike Massie

reviews.text: There's an appetite and a market out there for tongue-in-cheek spy extravaganzas, and this will probably run and run.
reviews.author: Peter Bradshaw

reviews.text: It comes off more as a chance director Matthew Vaughn had to make the WWI film of his dreams that happens to also be tied into a specific franchise.
reviews.author: Aaron Neuwirth

reviews.text: Weaving in and out of WWI, the third "Kingsman" film is as fancifully schlocky as its predecessors.
reviews.author: Owen Gleiberman

reviews.text: The King's Man is a joyless prequel to Kingsman, devoid of the charming offbeat comedy and pulse-pounding action scenes that made this franchise fun.
reviews.author: Molly Freeman

reviews.text: The King's Man isn't as good as the first one, an improvement over the sequel, but it is also its own thing at the same time. It's a bit too long, and the pacing is off, but there are some fantastic action scenes, and it's more fun than it isn't.
reviews.author: Kaitlyn Booth

reviews.text: The xenophobic subtext of the prior films in the Kingsman series is text in Matthew Vaughn's The King's Man.
reviews.author: Derek Smith

reviews.text: In an attempt to go more serious, The King's Man removes all the over-the-top action and shocking moments that made this franchise a fan favorite.
reviews.author: EJ Moreno

reviews.text: Trashy, deliberately and provocatively fun, The King's Man does for spy movies what The Suicide Squad did for superheroes.
reviews.author: Richard Trenholm

reviews.text: The result is something of a mixed bag, delivering plenty of thrilling action but not the same raucous sensibility that made the first film so much fun. All in all, The King's Man is a decent entertainment.
reviews.author: Sean Mulvihill

reviews.text: It's a film crammed with good starts to good ideas, only for them to end abruptly or go in directions that don't feel inevitable or thought through to their fullest potential.
reviews.author: Jon Negroni

reviews.text: A good old-fashioned British blockbuster that, while not flawless, delivers spy thrills and big surprises.
reviews.author: Ian Sandwell

synopsis: As a collection of history's worst tyrants and criminal masterminds gather to plot a war to wipe out millions, one man must race against time to stop them. Discover the origins of the very first independent intelligence agency in "The King's Man."
